finally to the consumers is called the national grid system.

The outermost energy level containing valence electrons splits more easily into many bands
than the inner levels. The most important bands in electronics are the valence and conduction
bands, which contain valence and conduction electrons respectively. The splitting of the energy
levels into bands and the inter-band distances dictate the electrical, optical and magnetic
properties of a given material. The energy gap between the conduction and valence bands is
called the forbidden energy gap and can be used to distinguish between insulators, conductors
and semiconductors.
